gloss: to cut corners, to slack off

definitions.gloss: to cut corners, to slack off, to do sloppy work
definitions.explanation: To not put in proper effort, doing something carelessly or incompletely to save time or effort.

examples.japanese: {手|て}を{抜|ぬ}いた{仕事|しごと}はすぐに{分|わ}かる。
examples.english: You can tell right away when work has been done sloppily.

examples.japanese: {忙|いそが}しいからといって{手|て}を{抜|ぬ}いてはいけない。
examples.english: You shouldn't cut corners just because you're busy.

examples.japanese: {料理|りょうり}では{絶対|ぜったい}に{手|て}を{抜|ぬ}かない。
examples.english: I never cut corners when cooking.

examples.japanese: {掃除|そうじ}で{手|て}を{抜|ぬ}いたのがバレた。
examples.english: They found out I did a sloppy job cleaning.

examples.japanese: あの{職人|しょくにん}は{何十年|なんじゅうねん}も{手|て}を{抜|ぬ}かずに{仕事|しごと}を{続|つづ}けてきた。だからこそ{信頼|しんらい}されている。
examples.english: That craftsman has continued working without cutting corners for decades. That's why he's trusted.

notes:
STRUCTURE: {手|て} (hand) + を + {抜|ぬ}く (to pull out/remove). The image is of removing one's hand from the work.

NUANCE: Generally negative - implies negligence or laziness. However, can occasionally be neutral when discussing efficiency or knowing where to save effort appropriately.

NEGATIVE FORM: {手|て}を{抜|ぬ}かない (to not cut corners) - often used positively
- 「{手|て}を{抜|ぬ}かない{職人|しょくにん}」(a craftsman who never cuts corners)

RELATED EXPRESSIONS:
- {手抜|てぬ}き (cutting corners, slipshod work) - noun form
- {手抜|てぬ}き{工事|こうじ} (shoddy construction work)
- いい{加減|かげん}な (half-hearted, sloppy)
- {適当|てきとう}にやる (to do carelessly)

OTHER {手|て} EXPRESSIONS:
- {手|て}が{離|はな}せない: too busy
- {手|て}を{焼|や}く: to have trouble with
- {手|て}を{打|う}つ: to take measures
